items.context: The item has no description. The title could mean several things: a scenario that estimates development effort for tasks, a test harness that measures how much agent effort (tokens, time, steps) tasks consume, or a placeholder/test item. Clarifying intent is the single most important unknown.

options.label: Effort estimation scenario
options.rationale: A tool/service that predicts how much work (time, complexity, story points) a task will take — useful for planning and prioritization in swarm-manager.

options.label: Agent effort measurement harness
options.rationale: A test framework that measures agent resource consumption (tokens, wall time, tool calls) per task — useful for optimizing agent performance and cost.

options.label: Placeholder / test item
options.rationale: This item was created to test backlog workflows and is not intended to become a real scenario. Can be archived.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe your intended purpose in the freeform field.

items.context: If this becomes a real scenario, understanding who benefits is key to scoping. Vrooli agents building other scenarios? Human developers planning sprints? The swarm-manager itself for scheduling decisions?

options.label: Vrooli agents (automated)
options.rationale: Agents use effort estimates to prioritize and schedule work autonomously via swarm-manager.

options.label: Human developers
options.rationale: Developers use effort estimates for sprint planning, capacity management, and stakeholder communication.

options.label: Both agents and humans
options.rationale: Dual interface — API for agents, UI/CLI for humans. More scope but more value.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe the target audience in the freeform field.

items.context: What delivery surfaces does this need? An API is the minimum for agent consumption. A CLI enables developer workflows. A UI enables richer interaction and visualization.

options.label: API only
options.rationale: Minimal surface area. Other scenarios and agents consume via HTTP. Fastest to build.

options.label: API + CLI
options.rationale: API for programmatic access, CLI for developer convenience. Moderate scope.

options.label: API + CLI + UI
options.rationale: Full scenario with all surfaces. Most useful but largest scope.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe your preferred components.

items.context: If this is an effort estimation tool, the approach matters significantly. Historical data from completed backlog items could train a model. Alternatively, LLM-based analysis of task descriptions could provide estimates without historical data.

options.label: Historical data analysis
options.rationale: Mine completed backlog items for actual effort data (time, commits, tokens). Requires sufficient history. Most accurate long-term.

options.label: LLM-based estimation
options.rationale: Use an LLM to analyze task descriptions and produce estimates. Works immediately but less calibrated. Could use Ollama.

options.label: Hybrid approach
options.rationale: Start with LLM estimates, calibrate against historical data as it accumulates. Best of both worlds but more complex.

options.label: Not applicable
options.rationale: Select if this isn't an estimation tool.

items.context: Which shared Vrooli resources would this scenario need? PostgreSQL for storing estimates and history. Ollama if using LLM-based estimation. Redis for caching.

options.label: PostgreSQL only
options.rationale: Minimal — store estimates and historical data. Sufficient for data-driven approaches.

options.label: PostgreSQL + Ollama
options.rationale: Storage plus local LLM for analysis. Enables AI-powered estimation without external API costs.

options.label: PostgreSQL + Ollama + Redis
options.rationale: Full stack — storage, AI, and caching. Best performance but more operational overhead.

options.label: None / minimal
options.rationale: If this is a test item or lightweight tool, it may not need persistent resources.

items.text: The swarm-manager already tracks backlog items with metadata (kind, priority, status, timestamps). If this becomes an effort estimation tool, it could integrate directly with swarm-manager's backlog API to pull task descriptions and push estimates back as metadata.
